content: MTA3, also known as Metastasis-associated protein 3, is a protein encoded by the MTA3 gene in humans. This protein is found in the nucleus as well as other cellular compartments. MTA3 is a component of the nucleosome remodeling and deacetylase (NuRD) complex, which plays a role in regulating gene expression. Interestingly, the expression pattern of MTA3 is inversely related to that of MTA1 and MTA2 during mammary gland tumorigenesis. However, MTA3 is also overexpressed in various human cancers. Mouse Mta3 was first identified as a partial cDNA with open reading frames during a screening of a mouse keratinocyte cDNA library using a human MTA1 partial fragment. This discovery was made by My G. Mahoney's research team. The full-length Mta3 cDNA was cloned using 5'-RACE methodology with RNA extracted from C57B1/6J mouse skin. The amino acid sequence of MTA3, when compared with sequences in the GenBank database, confirmed it as the third member of the MTA family. The MTA3 gene is located on chromosome 2p21 in humans and on chromosome 12p in mice. The human MTA3 gene contains 20 exons and produces 19 alternatively spliced transcripts. Of these, nine transcripts are predicted to encode six proteins of varying lengths (392, 514, 515, 537, 590, and 594 amino acids), while two transcripts encode shorter polypeptides of 18 and 91 amino acids. The remaining 10 transcripts are non-coding RNAs. In mice, the Mta3 gene produces nine transcripts, six of which encode proteins ranging from 251 to 591 amino acids, while one transcript encodes a 40-amino-acid polypeptide. The remaining two transcripts are predicted to be non-coding RNAs. The domain organization of the MTA3 protein is similar to other members of the MTA family. It contains a BAH (Bromo-Adjacent Homology) domain, an ELM2 (egl-27 and MTA1 homology) domain, a SANT (SWI, ADA2, N-CoR, TFIIB-B) domain, a GATA-like zinc finger domain, and a predicted bipartite nuclear localization signal (NLS). Additionally, the SH3 motif of MTA3 enables interactions with Fyn and Grb2, both of which are SH3-containing signaling proteins. The functions of MTA3 are believed to vary depending on the type of cancer. For instance, MTA3 expression is downregulated in breast cancer and endometrioid adenocarcinomas, while it is overexpressed in non-small cell lung cancer, human placenta, and choriocarcinoma cells. In breast cancer, the loss of MTA3 promotes epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT) and increases the invasiveness of cancer cells by upregulating Snail, which represses the E-cadherin adhesion molecule. In mammary epithelial and breast cancer cells, MTA3 is an estrogen-regulated gene and part of a larger regulatory network involving MTA1 and MTAs, which are modifiers of hormone response and participate in growth and differentiation processes. The MTA3-NuRD complex regulates the expression of Wnt4 in mammary epithelial cells and mice, controlling Wnt4-dependent ductal morphogenesis. In contrast to its repressive actions, MTA3 also stimulates the expression of HIF1α and its target genes under hypoxic conditions in trophoblasts, suggesting a role in differentiation during pregnancy. The MTA3-NuRD complex and its downstream targets have been implicated in primitive hematopoiesis and angiogenesis in zebrafish models. As part of the BCL6 corepressor complex, MTA3 regulates BCL6-dependent repression of target genes, including PRDM1, and modulates B-cell differentiation. The expression of MTA3 in breast cancer cells is stimulated by the estrogen receptor. The SP1 transcription factor also promotes MTA3 transcription. Conversely, microRNA-495 inhibits MTA3 mRNA levels and suppresses the growth and migration of non-small cell lung cancer cells. Additionally, β-elemene, a compound used in traditional Chinese medicine, upregulates MTA3 expression in breast cancer cells. The MTA3-NuRD complex represses Snail, a master regulator of epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT), as well as Wnt4 expression in mammary epithelial cells and BCL6-corepressor target genes. Furthermore, the MTA3-NuRD complex interacts with GATA3 to regulate the expression of GATA3 downstream targets. MTA3 also upregulates HIF1α and enhances its transactivation activity under hypoxic conditions.
